page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, configured with 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs via multithreading. Cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES. The instance contains 48.0 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is attached, requiring network-attached cloud storage, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily in the middle 50% across general computing, memory, and application operations. Multi-core execution demonstrates consistent mid-tier output, recorded at 10489.01 in stress-ng multi-core testing, 5870.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 11955.1 in PassMark CPU score. Memory performance aligns with expectations for enterprise DDR4 tiers, delivering 71.48 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 43.18 GB/sec in large-block write operations. Single-thread performance exhibits measurable constraints, with single-core stress-ng (1311.98) and single-threaded gzip compression (22.79 GB/sec) settling in the lower 25% distribution.

The 1:4 processor-to-memory allocation delivers balanced resource density without excess capacity overhead. The instance does not bundle hardware accelerators or ephemeral NVMe drives, avoiding the expense of unneeded physical components for workloads that rely exclusively on network-attached persistence. Application testing reveals reliable mid-tier throughput, including 10.32 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.06 GB/sec in static web serving. Workloads suited for this server include microservices tiers, enterprise web applications, container hosts, build servers, and relational database nodes that do not rely on local NVMe disk arrays.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.3xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by KVM, the configuration includes 48.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Supported instruction extensions include AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance carries no bundled local storage, requiring network block volumes, and operates with a 4 Gbps baseline network throughput. In synthetic benchmarks, multi-threaded CPU output, memory operations, and application tasks such as Redis processing (10.32 million SET ops/sec) sit firmly within the middle tier, whereas single-thread metrics skew toward the lower quartile. The balanced compute and memory profile aligns with web application servers, container hosting, standard database workloads, and build automation systems.
